title: "gsub() and {stringr} do not read the same regular expression"

categories: [Strings]
impact: incoherent
extrait: 'gsub("[\\d]", "", "a1b2d")'

::: {.piege packages="stringr"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(stringr))

x <- "a1b2d"
gsub("[\\d]", replacement = "", x = x)
str_remove_all(x, pattern = "[\\d]")

gsub("a(?=1)", replacement = "", x = x)
str_remove_all(x, pattern = "a(?=1)")
```
:::

## Why

R ships several regular expression engines. By default, `gsub()`, `grepl()` or `sub()` use TRE, which follows the POSIX standard. With `perl = TRUE`, they switch to PCRE. {stringr}, through {stringi}, uses ICU. Simple patterns behave the same everywhere, the others do not.

Inside square brackets, TRE reads `\d` as two literal characters, the backslash and the letter `d`: it removes the `d` and keeps the digits. ICU sees "a digit". TRE does not know lookarounds such as `(?=1)` either and returns an error, where ICU accepts them. Other differences exist: the non-breaking space, for instance, is a `\s` for ICU but not for TRE.

## The remedy

Stick to a single engine within a project. In base R, `perl = TRUE` gives a behaviour close to ICU. POSIX classes such as `[0-9]` or `[[:digit:]]` read the same everywhere.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
gsub("[\\d]", replacement = "", x = x, perl = TRUE)
gsub("a(?=1)", replacement = "", x = x, perl = TRUE)
gsub("[[:digit:]]", replacement = "", x = x)
```
:::
